package_metadata.name: napari-flopa
package_metadata.summary: Flim (fluorescence lifetime) image data opening, processing and analysis
package_metadata.description:
# napari-flopa [![License MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![npe2](https://img.shields.io/badge/plugin-npe2-blue)](https://napari.org/stable/plugins/index.html) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/napari-flopa.svg?color=green)](https://pypi.org/project/napari-flopa) [![Python Version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/napari-flopa.svg?color=green)](https://python.org) > **Work in progress** — the plugin is functional but under active development. Expect breaking changes between versions. A [napari] plugin for opening, processing and analysing FLIM (Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy) data from `.ptu` files. ## Feature panels - **File** - read a `.ptu`, display its header, reconstruct it into an xarray dataset (photon count, mean arrival time, phasor, TCSPC histogram) - supports multi-frame, multi-sequence (with line accumulation) and multi-detector data - bidirectional scans with an **Alignment wizard** for the line-marker delays - scan config with value provenance, saved/loaded as JSON - marker statistics - optional ROI mask to reconstruct only part of the field - **Drag and drop** — a `.ptu` or scan-config `.json` dropped onto napari opens in the File tab - **Trace** - photon-count time trace per detector over a chosen time window and bin width, with line/frame marker overlays - **FLIM View** (bottom dock) - intensity and lifetime display with histogram contrast sliders (Auto-once, Auto-live, Min-Max), smoothing - frame/sequence/detector selection or summing - lifetime *Calibrated* by the IRF delay from the phasor calibration - intensity, lifetime and combined masks as Labels layers - FLIM RGB composite - export to TIFF/PNG - **Phasor** - per-object or per-pixel phasor plot as scatter, intensity-weighted scatter or density (square or hex bins), smoothing - color by a Labels layer or use it as a filter - calibration from a reference lifetime or a custom factor - **Decay** - TCSPC decay curves with frame/sequence/detector aggregation, per-detector toggles, normalisation and log scale - **Batch** - process a folder (or selected files, opt. with sub-folders and label masks) with a shared scan config and calibration - export of images (FLIM RGB, intensity, lifetime), phasor tables per object or per pixel and decay tables (raw or normalised), per file or merged - **Analyzer** - explore phasor CSV tables (from Phasor or Batch) - color by any column - per-group density contours, mean/median and covariance ellipses - calibration - compute phase and modulation lifetimes - compute 2- and 3-component fractions - clustering (K-means, hierarchical; Gaussian mixture, DBSCAN, HDBSCAN with scikit-learn) - row filtering, regex grouping and column combining in **Data tools** ## Screenshots

File: ptu reading, header and scan configuration
Trace: photon-count time trace with marker overlays

FLIM View: lifetime over intensity visualization
Batch: batch processing with configurable outputs

Phasor: per object, colored by a Labels layer
Phasor: per pixel (here density color-coded & filtered by a mask)

Analyzer: tabular phasor data visualization
Analyzer: mono-exponential lifetime component fractions
## Requirements - Python ≥ 3.11 - [napari] with a Qt backend ## Installation **From PyPI - options** >```bash >pip install "napari-flopa[all]" # plugin + napari + Qt > ``` >```bash >pip install napari-flopa # plugin only, install into an existing napari >``` >```bash >pip install "napari-flopa[cluster]" # plugin only + scikit-learn >``` > The `cluster` extra adds scikit-learn for the Analyzer's Gaussian mixture, DBSCAN and >HDBSCAN clustering (K-means and hierarchical work without it). **From source** >```bash >git clone https://github.com/cockovaz/napari-flopa >cd napari-flopa >pip install -e ".[all]" # editable install, napari + Qt included >``` **Full install instructions** It is recommended to use virtual environment. See examples below. >uv > >```bash >uv venv --python 3.11 .venv >source .venv/bin/activate # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate >uv pip install "napari-flopa[all]" >``` > conda > >```bash >conda create -n flopa python=3.11 >conda activate flopa >pip install "napari-flopa[all]" >``` >pixi > >```bash >pixi init flopa >cd flopa >pixi add python=3.11 >pixi add --pypi "napari-flopa[all]" >``` ## Getting started 1. **Open the plugin** Start napari and choose **Plugins → FLOPA → FLIM Analysis**. 2. **Load a file** In the **File** tab, click **Load Demo** for the bundled demo dataset, or **Read PTU…** for your own — or drop a `.ptu` onto the napari window. > Note: the colored dot beside each field says where its value came from - file metadata, a default, an estimate, or your own edit. 3. **Set the scan geometry** Frames, lines, pixels, sequences and accumulations must match how the image was actually acquired, because the raw file is a stream of photon and marker events with no image shape of its own. The header contains some information, fill in the rest. **Demo dataset** is loaded with the correct configuration set up. **Marker Stats** inspects the marker events and suggests dimensions. For bidirectional scans, the **Alignment wizard** estimates the line-marker delays. 4. **Reconstruct** Pick what to compute under **Output**. Optionally pick an **ROI Mask** (a Labels layer or a mask file) to keep only the photons inside it. - *Intensity* — photon-count image only, the fastest - *Int. + τ* — adds the mean arrival time (lifetime) image - *All* — adds phasor coordinates per pixel and the global TCSPC decay (enables the **Phasor** and **Decay** tabs) 5. **Look at the result** The **FLIM View** dock opens at the bottom, with a histogram for Intensity and one for Lifetime. Each has two sliders: the **cyan** one sets the display contrast, the **red** one a threshold range. **→ Generate Int./Lt. Mask** turns that range into a napari Labels layer. Once a calibration is enabled in the Phasor tab, **Calibrated** shows the lifetime with the IRF delay subtracted (negative values are wrapped around by one period). Intensity, lifetime and the FLIM RGB composite can be exported from here. 6. **Analyze** - **Phasor** plots g/s per object or per pixel — apply a calibration factor, pick a Labels layer to color by object or to restrict the plot to a region. - **Decay** plots the global TCSPC curves per slice. **FLIM View** shows only decay of slice configuration currently shown in FLIM View. 7. **Reuse the settings** Use the **Batch** tab to run a whole folder of `.ptu` files with identical settings. Or export multiple slices of a single file. Each export pass picks frames, sequences and detectors as an index, `*` (all, one output per value) or `a` (aggregate). ## Data model Reading and reconstructing `.ptu` files is done by **[tttrkit]** (imported as `tttrkit.ptuio`), a separate package developed alongside this plugin. It is a normal dependency and is installed automatically — see [tttrkit] for the raw TTTR parsing, scan reconstruction and phasor maths that sit underneath the GUI. Reconstruction produces a single `xarray.Dataset` holding up to five variables. Four of them are images and share the dimensions `(frame, sequence, line, pixel, channel)`: `photon_count`, `mean_arrival_time`, `phasor_g` and `phasor_s`. Here `line` and `pixel` are the spatial axes and `channel` is the detector axis. The fifth, `tcspc_histogram`, is the global decay: its dimensions are `(frame, channel, tcspc_channel)` with no spatial axes. ## Roadmap Planned updates: - **Interactive phasor** — lasso a region of the plot and paint the matching pixels back into the image as a napari Labels layer - **Decay fitting** — extract lifetimes from the TCSPC curves - **Region-wise decay** — curves per mask and per object, not only per frame/detector - **Wider import support** — `.ptu` from further scanning systems, and other formats (`.sdt`, …) ## License Distributed under the terms of the [MIT] license. `napari-flopa` is free and open source software. ## Issues If you encounter any problems, please [file an issue] along with a detailed description. [napari]: https://github.com/napari/napari [tttrkit]: https://github.com/panekdal/tttrkit [MIT]: http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT [file an issue]: https://github.com/cockovaz/napari-flopa/issues [issues]: https://github.com/cockovaz/napari-flopa/issues [pip]: https://pypi.org/project/pip/
